sections.h2: Where is Westfield, MA, and how big is it?
sections.html:
Westfield is a Hampden County city in the Pioneer Valley of western Massachusetts, about 10 miles west of Springfield and 95 miles west of Boston. It is large by land, at 47.31 square miles, with 40,834 residents in the 2020 Census, so it has far more open ground per person than a city like Watertown.

The Westfield River splits it into the North Side and the South Side, and the northwest corner is known as Wyben. Neighbors include Southampton, Holyoke, West Springfield, Agawam, Southwick, Granville, Russell and Montgomery.

The 2020 Census found 15,887 households and 16,869 housing units, with 5.8% of units vacant. The median resident was 40.6 years old, and 19.1% of residents were 65 or older.

sections.h2: Why is Westfield called the Whip City?
sections.html:
Westfield earned the nickname from the buggy whip trade that made it a manufacturing center in the nineteenth century. Early settlers farmed the river's alluvial soil for about 150 years, and in the 1800s the city added bricks, whips, cigars, bicycles, paper products, pipe organs, boilers, radiators and precision tools.

Westfield was first settled in 1660, became a town in 1669 and a city on November 2, 1920. It was the westernmost settlement in the Massachusetts colony until 1725. In 1939 it elected Alice Burke, the first woman mayor in Massachusetts and in New England. Manufacturing eroded in the second half of the twentieth century, and the north side turned to warehousing, with C&S Wholesale, Home Depot and Lowes listed among the operators.

sections.h2: Is Westfield prone to flooding, and what does the climate mean for a house?
sections.html:
Westfield sits in a floodplain zone and Wikipedia describes the city as flood-prone. The Westfield River drops out of the Berkshire Hills with a large, steep, rocky watershed, so it has a history of severe floods in the adjoining neighborhoods. Pumps, dikes, waterways and upstream dams help, but they do not remove the risk.

Winters are cold. At Westfield-Barnes Regional Airport the January mean high is about 33 degrees and the mean low about 13, and the record low is 20 below zero. Annual precipitation averages 48.39 inches.

  • Ask your insurer whether your address is in a mapped flood zone.
  • Keep records of any basement water, sump repairs or storm claims.
  • Service the heating system before showings, since buyers test it in winter.

sections.h2: What schools, hospitals and college are in Westfield?
sections.html:
Westfield Public Schools run one preschool, five elementary schools, an intermediate school, a middle school and two high schools, Westfield High School and Westfield Technical Academy. The 2024-25 enrollment was 4,772. Westfield River Elementary School opened on January 6, 2025, replacing Franklin Avenue and Abner Gibbs.

Westfield State University anchors the south side, and students make up roughly 15 percent of the population. Baystate Noble Hospital and the state-run Western Massachusetts Hospital are the two main hospitals.

sections.h2: How do roads, buses and airports serve Westfield?
sections.html:
The Massachusetts Turnpike (I-90) crosses just north of Westfield Center and meets I-91 about three miles east. U.S. 20 is the main east-west street, and U.S. 202 and Route 10 run north and south. The Great River Bridge over the Westfield River, called the Green Bridge, was doubled in the 2000s so each span carries one direction.

Pioneer Valley Transit Authority routes R10 and B23 connect to Springfield, West Springfield and Holyoke. Passenger trains no longer stop in the city. The nearest Amtrak and CTrail Hartford Line service is in Springfield, 9.6 miles east, and Bradley International Airport in Windsor Locks is 18 miles south. Westfield-Barnes Regional Airport offers charter service.

sections.h2: What should Westfield owners know about property tax abatements?
sections.html:
Westfield follows the same state procedure as every Massachusetts city. An abatement lowers a bill when the assessed value exceeds fair cash value, when an exemption applies, or when the classification is wrong. The burden of proof sits with the taxpayer, and the strongest evidence is recent sales of similar nearby houses.

  • File the abatement application with the assessors by the first installment due date.
  • The assessors have three months to decide.
  • The Appellate Tax Board hears appeals filed within three months of the decision.
  • Most single-family appeals use the informal procedure, which has no formal discovery.

Westfield's assessor posts local forms and deadlines. Check them with that office, because the state guide gives only general timing.

sections.h2: What parks, trails and public spaces sit near Westfield homes?
sections.html:
Westfield has a lot of green space for a city its size, and a buyer will notice it. Wikipedia lists Stanley Park, Amelia Park Ice Rink and Memorial Garden, the Columbia Greenway Rail Trail, East Mountain and the 114-mile Metacomet-Monadnock Trail, which crosses the city. The Westfield Athenaeum, a free public library, has served the city since 1868.

The City Council meets on the first and third Thursday of each month at 7:30 p.m. in City Hall, which is where zoning and ordinance questions end up. Wikipedia also notes a mitigation action over PFAS in the city's water. If your house has a private well, ask the local health office about testing before you list.

sections.h2: What are the closing costs for a Westfield seller?
sections.html:
Westfield deeds are recorded at the Hampden County Registry of Deeds, which charges $155 to record a deed and applies an excise tax of $4.56 per $1,000 of taxable value. The registry accepts cash and checks only.

At that rate a $250,000 sale carries $1,140 in deed excise. A recorded municipal lien certificate costs $80 there. Your lender payoff, title work and any agent fee come on top, so ask the closing attorney for an itemized estimate before you accept an offer.

sections.h2: Selling a Westfield house fast: your realistic options
sections.html:
Westfield owners usually weigh three paths. A listing can bring the strongest price when the house shows well. A private sale saves the commission but needs paperwork help. A cash sale closes quickly and skips the repair list.

For an inherited house, a flood-damaged basement or a home with tenants, speed and certainty often matter more than squeezing out the last dollar. Compare written offers, keep the closing date flexible, and ask each buyer how they handle title questions or an unpaid tax bill that has to be cleared at closing.

faqs.q: How many people live in Westfield, MA?
faqs.a: The 2020 Census counted 40,834 residents, and a 2024 estimate puts the figure near 40,403.

faqs.q: Is Westfield, MA in a floodplain?
faqs.a: Parts of the city lie in the Westfield River floodplain, and the city is considered flood-prone despite dikes and dams. Confirm your own address on the FEMA flood map and with your insurer.

faqs.q: What is the deed excise tax for a Westfield sale?
faqs.a: The Hampden County Registry of Deeds lists $4.56 per $1,000 of taxable value or fraction of $1,000, with no tax when the stated price is under $100.
Westfield State University is in the city, and students make up about 15 percent of the population according to Wikipedia.

faqs.q: When does the Westfield City Council meet?
faqs.a: Wikipedia reports meetings on the first and third Thursday of each month at 7:30 p.m. in City Hall. Confirm the current schedule with the city clerk.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Westfield house that has water damage?
faqs.a: Yes. You can list it with disclosures, sell it to an investor or take a cash offer from a company that buys as is. Describe the damage honestly in writing so nothing surprises the buyer at closing.
